Coach's summary

What went well

  • Race 1: first to every mark, 56 s ahead at the finish
  • Race 5: first to the windward mark
  • Roundings: best leeward roundings of the three boats, 55 m (5.9 lengths) lost toward the marks on average
  • Runs in Races 1–2: 43 s gained on 969

Top priorities

  1. Upwind: higher and slower than 969, and 969 got to the mark first, both days
    Next time: When the boat beside you is footing away, match it: bear off 1–2° and build speed. In the chop, power up the way the Worlds leaders did (traveller up, more twist, deeper jib foot). In light air, ease to flatten and keep the boat moving. It only counts if the gap to the mark stops growing, so judge it against the boat beside you, not the speedo.
  2. Starts: late on Saturday, slow on Sunday
    Next time: Three timed runs along the line before the start, with a burn time that gets re-called up to the gun. Hold speed until the bow says two lengths, then kill it, and be sheeting on at −8 s. In light air, start the build a few seconds earlier: the boat takes longer to get going.
  3. Runs: fastest over the ground but not to the mark, in Races 3 and 4
    Next time: On a run, sail the angle that gets you to the gate, not the one that feels fast. Gybe on the shifts and pressure, not to get back to the rhumb line.

Debrief

The coaching debrief.

Sept ODW (Mojo): Sat 26 and Sun 27 Sep 2026, 5 races

  • Saturday: 3 races in the breeze, about 5.8 kt upwind over the ground. Sunday: 2 races, light and dying, 4.7 kt upwind in Race 4 and 3.3 kt in Race 5. Wind 263–294° magnetic by our compass. There's no wind sensor.
  • Among the three tracked boats (with 969 and 1216), we were 1, 3, 3, 3, 2. That's 12 points, level with 1216 and ahead of it on time, and 9:54 behind the first tracked boat over the five races.
  • Where the time went: 33 s at the starts, 443 s upwind and 118 s downwind. Race 5's last beat alone was 275 s of the upwind.
  • Everything below is judged on getting to the mark: time between marks and VMC (speed toward the mark). Speed and heel only explain it.

What went well

  • Race 1: first to every mark, 56 s ahead at the finish
    • Pin start 1 s late at 5.8 kt, 2 m (0.2 lengths) behind the line at the gun: the Worlds standard.
    • First beat 20 s faster than 969's: VMC 4.37 kt to the mark, against 4.28 kt.
  • Race 5: first to the windward mark
    • The first beat was the fastest of the three boats: 17:44, VMC 2.68 kt, against 969's 2.61 kt. We sailed the least distance (1.10 nm against 1.18–1.19 nm).
  • Roundings: best leeward roundings of the three boats, 55 m (5.9 lengths) lost toward the marks on average
    • Race 5's leeward rounding was our best, and Race 4's windward 2 cost only 36 m (3.9 lengths).
  • Runs in Races 1–2: 43 s gained on 969

Top 3 to work on

  1. Upwind: higher and slower than 969, and 969 got to the mark first, both days
    • Side by side, 969 gained 88 m (9.5 lengths) toward the mark in 33 minutes on Saturday, and 103 m (11 lengths) in 19 minutes on Sunday. Both days 969 was faster (+143 m (15 lengths) and +146 m (16 lengths) from speed) and lower (−55 m (5.9 lengths) and −43 m (4.6 lengths) from course). The footing paid.
    • Sunday's upwind SOG was the slowest of the three boats (4.66 and 3.28 kt, against 969's 4.90 and 3.64 kt), with the most heel (12.4° and 8.8°, against 11.2° and 8.2°). On Saturday we had the least heel. Heel isn't the answer on its own: the mode is.
    • Next time: When the boat beside you is footing away, match it: bear off 1–2° and build speed. In the chop, power up the way the Worlds leaders did (traveller up, more twist, deeper jib foot). In light air, ease to flatten and keep the boat moving. It only counts if the gap to the mark stops growing, so judge it against the boat beside you, not the speedo.
  2. Starts: late on Saturday, slow on Sunday
    • Race 2: 15 s late, 31 m (3.3 lengths) back at the gun, at 4.8 kt. Race 3: 24 s late, 17 m (1.8 lengths) back, at 3.8 kt, after slowing from 6.4 kt at −30 s to 2.4 kt at −10 s.
    • Sunday: 6–7 s late and 7.5–8.8 m (0.8–0.9 lengths) back, at 4.7 and 4.0 kt. That's not full speed, even in light air.
    • The Worlds leaders on this same water were 1–2 m (0.1–0.2 lengths) behind the line at full speed. Race 1 met that standard, and it was our only win. In Race 3 we were at the favoured pin (worth about 34 m (3.7 lengths)) but slow, so the bias was lost.
    • Next time: Three timed runs along the line before the start, with a burn time that gets re-called up to the gun. Hold speed until the bow says two lengths, then kill it, and be sheeting on at −8 s. In light air, start the build a few seconds earlier: the boat takes longer to get going.
  3. Runs: fastest over the ground but not to the mark, in Races 3 and 4
    • Race 3: 6.06 kt against 969's 5.79, but VMC to the gate was only 4.99 kt against 5.39. We sailed 1.16 nm to 969's 1.02: 51 s lost.
    • Race 4, first run: 4.90 kt, the fastest of the three, but 1.34 nm sailed to 969's 1.20. That was 34 s lost to 969.
    • Next time: On a run, sail the angle that gets you to the gate, not the one that feels fast. Gybe on the shifts and pressure, not to get back to the rhumb line.

Also worth a look:

  • Race 4, first beat: 1:49 lost to 1216 and 54 s to 969
    • The wind went 15° left two minutes after the start and kept backing (25° in all by the top). We worked the right (80% of the beat right of the rhumb line), with 6 tacks. 1216 was out on the left when it came.
  • Race 5, last beat: 4:35 lost to 969 in a dying right shift
    • The wind went 20–35° right as it faded. 969 went right first and stayed there. We went right, then sailed the lifted starboard tack back to the left while the wind was still going right. See the Race 5 wind chart on the fleet page.
  • Race 2, second windward rounding: 79 m (8.5 lengths) lost toward the marks
    • 27 m (2.9 lengths) of it in the 30 s before the mark (pinching up to it), then 50 s to settle on the run.

What the wind did, and where we were (from all three boats' GPS tracks, so no compass error; magnetic)

  • Race 1, beat 1: the left paid, and we were on it. The wind went 16° left (273° to 258°). We were the least far right of the three, fastest up the beat, and gained 29 s on 1216, which was 220 m further right. The shift alone was worth about 26 s. The pin start set that up.
  • Races 2 and 3: no side paid. Steady or oscillating (±4°). The 47 s lost on Race 3's first beat and 51 s on its run were speed and distance, not the wind.
  • Race 4, beat 1: the new wind came on the left, and we went right. 15° left at two minutes, 25° by the top. We started mid-line (42%), about 150 m right of 1216, and tacked onto port with everyone at about two minutes. When 1216 went furthest left, it gained 56 s on 969, the furthest right; the shift alone was worth about 53 s.
  • Race 5, last beat: we left the new wind. From about 35 minutes the wind went right, from 280° to 304–316°. We were 280 m right by 38 minutes, then tacked back across to the left (200 m left by 50 minutes) on the lifted starboard tack while it was still right. 969 stayed right and gained 4:35.
  • Next time: A shift of 10° or more that holds for two or three minutes is the new wind, not an oscillation. Get to that side (sail the header toward it first) before you tack back. In a dying breeze, the side the wind is going to usually has the pressure too.

Upwind vs. targets

  • Not computed: we don't have a wind speed. 969 is the benchmark instead, measured by who got to the mark first (see the fleet debrief).

Race notes

  • Race 1: A clean pin start and the fastest first beat of the day. First of the tracked boats, by 56 s.
  • Race 2: Late start in the middle of the line and 42 s down at the first mark. The second beat cost 33 s more, then that rounding lost 79 m (8.5 lengths) toward the marks. Third.
  • Race 3: Late at the pin, then 47 s lost upwind and 51 s on the run from extra distance. Third, 10 s behind 1216.
  • Race 4: Went right on the first beat while the wind went left: 1:52 behind 1216 and 55 s behind 969 at the first mark. After that we gained 37 s on 1216 and lost 55 s more to 969. Third.
  • Race 5: Led at the first mark. Lost the lead to 969 on the run (35 s), then 4:35 on the last beat in the dying right shift. Second, ahead of 1216.

Data notes

  • VMC: speed toward the next mark, measured up the ladder at the boats' own tacking or gybing angle (overstanding counts against it). SOG is over the ground.
  • There's no wind channel. Wind direction is estimated from our tacking headings. The TWS in the files is a smooth modelled value, not a measurement, so it isn't used.
  • Race 5's data runs to 22:05, because Njord's race end (21:42:46) came before anyone finished.
  • Only Mojo, 969 and 1216 were tracked, so the order and gaps here are between those boats, not race results.

Three questions

  • In Race 3, what happened between −30 s and −10 s? 1216 slowed the same way (6.5 kt to 2.3 kt) right beside you at the pin. Were you blocked, or was that a deliberate stall?
  • Were the runs along the line before each start timed, and who owns the burn time?
  • What was the call on the Race 4 first beat? The right looked good at the start, or was it a lane?

Summary

The whole event at a glance, then each day and each race.

Executive summary

Overall: 5 races; wind 263–294° magnetic; starts 1–24 s late; heel 9–19°; 22 tacks away from the marks: 7 on headers, 3 on lifts; worked the right on 8 of 10 beats (3 beats trended left, 2 right); laylines 7 good / 2 overstood; windward roundings 39 m (4.2 lengths) lost on average (8 roundings); leeward roundings 55 m (5.9 lengths) lost on average (5 roundings).

Sat 26 Sep

Day: 3 races; wind 264–270° magnetic; starts 1–24 s late; heel 18–19°; 13 tacks away from the marks: 2 on headers, 1 on lifts; worked the right on 5 of 6 beats (2 beats trended left, 0 right); laylines 6 good / 0 overstood; windward roundings 32 m (3.4 lengths) lost on average (5 roundings); leeward roundings 61 m (6.6 lengths) lost on average (3 roundings).

  • Race 1 (12:55, 50 min): Start 1 s late, pin end, slowing (-0.6 kt); upwind VMC 4.33 kt to the mark (SOG 5.87 kt), heel 19°; downwind VMC 6.26 kt to the mark (SOG 6.50 kt); 7 tacks (30% speed loss), 0 tacks on a header vs 0 on a lift; beats: trending left 6° (we went right), trending left 5° (we went left). Flags: leg 1: wind went left, we went right.
  • Race 2 (14:05, 51 min): Start 15 s late, middle, slowing (-0.4 kt); upwind VMC 4.28 kt to the mark (SOG 5.82 kt), heel 19°; downwind VMC 6.04 kt to the mark (SOG 6.38 kt); 9 tacks (29% speed loss), 0 tacks on a header vs 1 on a lift; beats: steady (we went right), steady (we went right). Flags: late start (15 s); windward rounding #3 lost 79 m (8.5 lengths).
  • Race 3 (15:15, 39 min): Start 24 s late, pin end, flat (+0.3 kt); upwind VMC 4.21 kt to the mark (SOG 5.67 kt), heel 18°; downwind VMC 4.99 kt to the mark (SOG 6.16 kt); 10 tacks (34% speed loss), 2 tacks on a header vs 0 on a lift; beats: oscillating (we went right), oscillating (we went right). Flags: late start (24 s); leeward rounding #2 lost 68 m (7.3 lengths).

Sun 27 Sep

Day: 2 races; wind 263–294° magnetic; starts 6–7 s late; heel 9–12°; 9 tacks away from the marks: 5 on headers, 2 on lifts; worked the right on 3 of 4 beats (1 beat trended left, 2 right); laylines 1 good / 2 overstood; windward roundings 51 m (5.5 lengths) lost on average (3 roundings); leeward roundings 46 m (4.9 lengths) lost on average (2 roundings).

  • Race 4 (12:30, 64 min): Start 6 s late, middle, slowing (-0.6 kt); upwind VMC 3.29 kt to the mark (SOG 4.66 kt), heel 12°; downwind VMC 4.03 kt to the mark (SOG 5.06 kt); 9 tacks (40% speed loss), 2 tacks on a header vs 2 on a lift; beats: trending left 11° (we went right), steady (we went right). Flags: 2 laylines overstood; deep tacks (40% loss); windward rounding #1 lost 66 m (7.0 lengths); leg 1: wind went left, we went right.
  • Race 5 (14:00, 53 min): Start 7 s late, middle, flat (-0.1 kt); upwind VMC 2.31 kt to the mark (SOG 3.29 kt), heel 9°; downwind VMC 3.79 kt to the mark (SOG 4.25 kt); 7 tacks (42% speed loss), 3 tacks on a header vs 0 on a lift; beats: trending right 16° (we went right), trending right 48° (we went middle). Flags: deep tacks (42% loss).

Tacks

Every comparable tack, lined up at head to wind (0 s): the moment the heading is halfway through the turn. The best 10% by time lost are drawn in the boat's colour and the rest in grey. Time lost is what the turn itself cost toward the mark: the dip in VMC (speed toward the mark) from 5 s before to 25 s after, against a line from the VMC going in to the VMC once settled, in seconds. What changing tack was worth (onto a lift, or off it) is the call, shown separately, so a tack isn't ranked well just for leaving a bad heading. Speed (SOG) explains a tack; VMC scores it. Click a line, dot or table row to follow one tack.

Speed through the tack

Heading through the tack

Degrees turned from the settled heading before the tack (−14 to −8 s). Where a line settles is the tacking angle; a hump above it is overshoot past the new course.

Tacking angle vs time lost

Over the ground is from GPS course and doesn't depend on the compass. The gap between it and the compass angle is leeway through the tack (both tacks' leeway added together).

Keeping roundings tight

The goal is zero metres lost. These are the habits behind a tight rounding; the suggestions under each rounding below say which ones that rounding missed.

  • Windward, on the layline: tack onto it with room to sail the last 100 m at full speed, not pinching up to the mark and not overstood. Pole and halyard ready before the mark.
  • Windward, the bear-away: ease main and vang and turn steadily all the way to the run angle, then hoist. Reaching off high first and setting there is where our slowest exits went.
  • Leeward, the approach: drop early enough that the turn starts before the mark. Enter wide, a couple of boat lengths out, so the turn can finish right at the mark.
  • Leeward, the exit: tight out, about a boat length from the mark, with main and jib trimmed on through the turn. Foot at your normal upwind angle until the speed is back, then point.
  • Both: one smooth radius, helm and trim together. The bigger the speed dip, the longer it takes to get it back.

Current

Course over ground against heading: how far the boats were set sideways, and where on the course. Each boat's compass offset is taken out first, so boats with different compasses can share one map.

What COG − heading is made of

The gap between course over ground and heading adds up three things: the compass offset (the same on every heading), leeway (upwind, to leeward) and current. Without a paddlewheel, current running along the wind can't be told apart from leeway, so upwind the two are reported together as slip. Between boats in the same water, a difference in slip is a difference in leeway. Current across the course can be measured, and so can where the set was stronger.

Tack to tack: speed and drift

A current across the course makes one tack faster over the ground and the other slower, and pushes both tracks the same way. Comparing port with starboard on the same leg, for the same boat, takes the compass out of the speed test completely (each boat's compass is calibrated differently). Real current shows up on every boat, holds from a beat to the run after it, and agrees with the drift. Waves or pressure on one tack don't.

Each dot is one boat on one leg: its median SOG on starboard minus port (steady sailing only). Circles: beats; diamonds: runs. Hover for the current across the course each would imply, and what the drift says.

Metres toward the mark. Handling: the dip against a baseline from the VMC before to the VMC once settled after (what the turn itself cost). Wind direction from headings: heading ± half the tacking angle. Shifts are relative to each beat's median; + is a right shift (veer), − a left shift (back). A puff that lets the boat point higher also reads as a lift, so treat single 3–4° calls as soft.

Metres toward the mark. Handling: the dip against a baseline from the VMC before to the VMC once settled after (what the turn itself cost). Call: what changing onto the new tack's VMC was worth over the same 30 s (negative = gained, e.g. tacking off a header). They add up to the total against keeping the VMC it had.

Wind shifts and tack calls

Wind direction from headings: heading ± half the tacking angle. Shifts are relative to each beat's median; + is a right shift (veer), − a left shift (back). A puff that lets the boat point higher also reads as a lift, so treat single 3–4° calls as soft.

Mark roundings

Metres lost toward the marks: VMC (speed toward this mark, then the next) from 30 s before to 60 s after the rounding against the steady VMC of the leg before and after. Settled: 10 s VMC back to 90% of the next leg's.

  • #1 windward: Reached off at 131° to the wind for the first 15–40 s after the mark (your best exited at 166°). Bear away all the way to the run angle first, then set. Took 47 s to settle on the run (best 16 s). Pole and halyard ready on the layline, so the set happens as you bear away. Gave away 16 m (1.7 lengths) in the 30 s before the mark. Keep target speed on the layline; don't pinch up to the mark.
  • #2 leeward: Your best of this type so far: the benchmark to beat. The goal is still zero. Tacked 57 s after the mark, so its cost is in this number. Fine if it was for clear air or the favoured side; otherwise hold the lane until you're up to speed.
